does: Steeps food in a seasoned liquid before it is cooked, so that its surface takes on the flavour.

intro.what: Marinating coats food in a seasoned liquid before cooking so the surface takes on flavour.
intro.why: It teaches you to separate surface flavouring from the later dry browning step.

how: Mix the wine or the acid with the aromatics and a little oil.
Turn the food in it until it is coated, in a bowl that acid does not attack.
Cover it and keep it in the fridge, turning it once or twice.
Lift the food out and dry it well before browning it. Keep the marinade for the pot.

cues.text: Meat from a wine marinade is stained on the outside. The colour does not reach far inside.
The meat smells of the wine and the herbs.

mistakes.mistake: Browning meat straight from the marinade, wet, so that it steams and will not colour.
mistakes.fix: Drain it and pat it dry first.

mistakes.mistake: Expecting a marinade to make a tough cut tender.
mistakes.fix: It flavours the surface. Only long, gentle cooking makes a tough cut tender.

quiz.question: What does this marinade primarily flavour?
choices: Every part equally far into a thick piece.
Only the liquid, leaving the food unchanged.
quiz.because: The visible staining and scent concentrate at the surface rather than reaching far inside.

quiz.question: How do you distribute the seasoned liquid?
choices: Turn the food until coated, then cover and refrigerate.
Leave part of the food dry above the liquid throughout.
Dry the food before its first contact with the marinade.
quiz.because: Turning gives the surfaces contact with the seasoned liquid before the covered rest.

quiz.question: What might you see on meat lifted from a wine marinade?
choices: Identical deep colour through the whole piece.
Surface staining that does not reach far inside.
A browned crust already formed by the marinade.
quiz.because: Wine can stain the outside, illustrating the surface-focused effect of marinating.

quiz.question: Wet marinated meat steams instead of browning. What would you change next time?
choices: Pour extra marinade into the browning pan.
Cover the pan to retain the surface moisture.
Drain and pat it dry before browning.
quiz.because: Removing surface moisture lets the browning step proceed instead of steaming the wet meat.
